key_insight: Calibrated XGBoost performed best among the evaluated models for classifying documented suicide-related outcomes in an age-matched EHR cohort.
clinical_relevance: EHR-derived clinical and social-contextual features may support suicide-related risk research, but these findings do not establish readiness for clinical screening.
method: Used MIMIC-IV diagnosis categories to define features and a composite suicide-related outcome.
Retained all positive patients and age-matched comparison patients to address imbalance and reduce age confounding.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost with isotonic calibration; used SHAP for interpretation.
evidence_signal: In retrospective MIMIC-IV evaluation, calibrated XGBoost showed the strongest matched-cohort performance; the abstract reports no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Code-based outcomes capture documented events, not necessarily future risk; external validation and evaluation at real-world prevalence are needed.
paper_title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
